intro.title: Build CQRS split read write endpoints basics
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Node.js API that separates read and write operations using the CQRS (Command Query Responsibility Segregation) pattern. You will learn how to create distinct endpoints: one for handling commands (write operations) and another for handling queries (read operations). The core programming concepts involve structuring your application logic to isolate data modifications from data retrieval, improving scalability and maintainability. You will use Express.js to set up the server, define routes, and handle HTTP requests with clear separation of concerns. By the end, you'll have a basic understanding of how to implement CQRS in a Node.js application to manage different types of requests efficiently.
intro.usecase: The CQRS pattern is essential in modern applications where read and write operations have vastly different performance requirements. For example, in e-commerce platforms like Amazon, product listing pages (reads) need to handle millions of queries with complex filtering, while checkout processes (writes) require transactional integrity for inventory updates. Social media feeds separate read-heavy timeline displays from write operations like posting or liking content. This separation allows developers to optimize databases independently—using fast read replicas for queries and dedicated write databases for commands—ensuring scalability and responsiveness in high-traffic applications.

objectives: Construct separate Express.js routes for read and write operations
Initialize distinct data structures to isolate read and write models
Implement a write endpoint that processes and stores command data
Configure a read endpoint that retrieves data from the query model
Manipulate the application structure to enforce CQRS separation
Integrate the split endpoints into a single Node.js application
Apply CQRS principles by updating the write model to synchronize with the read model

steps.instruction: Create a function named parseRequestBody that takes a request object as a parameter and returns a promise that resolves with the parsed JSON body.
steps.hint: You'll need to read the request data in chunks, collect it, and then parse it as JSON. Use the request's 'data' and 'end' events.
steps.expectedOutcome: A reusable function that can parse JSON from incoming HTTP requests.
successCriteria: The parseRequestBody function is defined, takes a request parameter, returns a promise, and handles reading and parsing JSON.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.feedbackWrong: The function doesn't seem to parse the request body correctly. Review how to read data from the request stream and parse JSON.

steps.instruction: Create a function named handleAddItem that takes a request and response object as parameters and handles POST requests to add new items to the data store.
steps.hint: Define a function that checks if the request method is POST, parses the request body, creates a new item object with an ID and the parsed data, pushes it to the items array, and sends a JSON response.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named handleAddItem is created that will handle POST requests to add items to the in-memory store.
successCriteria: The handleAddItem function is defined with req and res parameters and contains logic for handling POST requests.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started creating the handler function, but make sure it's named handleAddItem and accepts both req and res parameters.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't properly defined. Create a function named handleAddItem that takes req and res parameters to handle POST requests.

steps.expectedOutcome: A handleGetItems function is defined that will handle GET requests by returning all items from the data store.
successCriteria: The handleGetItems function is created, sets the correct Content-Type header, and returns the items array as JSON.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created the function, but make sure it sets the Content-Type header to 'application/json' and returns the items array using JSON.stringify.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function is missing or incorrect. Remember to create a function named handleGetItems that takes req and res parameters, sets the response header, and sends the items array as JSON.

steps.instruction: Create a function named handleGetItem that takes request and response objects as parameters and handles GET requests to fetch a single item by ID from the URL.
steps.hint: Extract the ID from the URL path, find the matching item in the items array, and send the item as JSON if found, or a 404 error if not found.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleGetItem function is added that can retrieve a single item by ID from the in-memory store.
successCriteria: The handleGetItem function is defined, extracts an ID from the URL, finds the matching item, and returns appropriate JSON responses for success and error cases.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the function, but make sure it extracts the ID from the URL, finds the item, and handles both success (200) and not-found (404) cases with proper JSON responses.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function is missing or incomplete. Review the example: handleGetItem should parse the ID from the URL, search the items array, and send appropriate JSON responses.

steps.title: Create main request router function
steps.instruction: Create a function named handleRequest that takes request and response objects as parameters, examines the request method and URL, and routes to the correct handler function.
steps.hint: Inside the function, use if/else or switch statements to check request.method and request.url, then call the appropriate handler function you created earlier.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a handleRequest function that can route incoming HTTP requests to the appropriate handler functions based on the request method and URL path.
successCriteria: The handleRequest function is defined, takes req and res parameters, and contains logic to route requests to the correct handler functions.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the handleRequest function, but it needs to examine both the request method and URL to route to the correct handlers. Make sure you're calling the handler functions you created earlier.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleRequest function is missing or doesn't properly route requests. Remember to check both request.method and request.url, then call the appropriate handler function.

steps.title: Create HTTP server with request handling
steps.instruction: Create the HTTP server instance using the http module's createServer method, passing your handleRequest function as the request handler.
steps.hint: Call http.createServer() with your router function as the argument, then assign it to a constant variable.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server instance is created and configured to use your handleRequest function for routing all incoming requests.
successCriteria: An HTTP server instance is created using http.createServer() with handleRequest as the request handler.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling http.createServer() and passing your handleRequest function as the argument.
steps.feedbackWrong: The server instance wasn't created correctly. Remember to use http.createServer() with your handleRequest function as the request handler.

steps.expectedOutcome: The server will be configured to listen for incoming requests on port 3000 and log a confirmation message when started.
successCriteria: The server.listen method is called with port 3000 and a callback that logs a startup message.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the server, but make sure to include a callback function that logs a startup message.
steps.feedbackWrong: The server isn't configured to listen yet. Use server.listen with port 3000 and a callback.

steps.title: Add error handling for the server
steps.instruction: Add an error event listener to the server to handle common errors like address already in use.
steps.hint: Use the server.on('error', ...) method to listen for error events and handle them appropriately.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server will now handle errors gracefully, such as when the port is already in use.
successCriteria: Server has an error event listener that handles at least the EADDRINUSE error.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added an error listener, but make sure it handles specific error cases like EADDRINUSE.
steps.feedbackWrong: The server still needs error handling. Add an error event listener to handle common server errors.
